newsitem.title: CANADA: Tee-Comm says U.S. service growing.
newsitem.headline: Tee-Comm says U.S. service growing.

text.p: Tee-Comm Electronics Inc is signing up some 250 new subscribers a day for its new home satellite television service in the United States, company chief financial officer Jim Wilkinson said on Tuesday.

Wilkinson said the number of people signing up continues to increase for the service that was launched through its Alpha Star subsidiary. He said the company's target is to sign up 940 new subscribers per day.
Tee-Comm has 12,000 subscribers for the AlphaStar Television Network that was launched in the quarter after beta testing in July.

Wilkinson said matters were proceeding well on its application by subsidiary AlphaStar Canada for a home satellite television service in Canada. The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission has scheduled public hearings on the AlphaStar Canada application for Dec. 2, 1996.

Tee-Comm reported revenue for the third quarter rose to C$16,290,000 to C$8,918,000 in the third quarter of 1995. For the first nine months of 1996, revenue was C$25,041,000 down from C$30,868,000 in 1995.
Tee-Comm reported a net loss of C$16,998,000 for the quarter and a loss of C$23,830,000 for the year to date.
